*(Note: Calculations based on standard AC parallel/series branch parameters visible in typical Fig 2 setups)*

(i) **RMS Line Current ($I_{rms}$)**:
Calculated by finding the total impedance $Z_{total}$ of the network connected across supply voltage $V$:
$$I_{rms} = \frac{V}{Z_{total}}$$

(ii) **Power Dissipated ($P$)**:
Power is consumed only by the resistive components:
$$P = V_{rms} \cdot I_{rms} \cdot \cos\phi = I_{rms}^2 \cdot R_{eq}$$

(iii) **Power Factor ($\cos\phi$)**:
Given by the ratio of resistance to impedance or active power to apparent power:
$$\cos\phi = \frac{R_{eq}}{Z_{total}} = \frac{P}{S}$$
proTip: Always use complex impedance notation ($\bar{Z} = R + jX$) for AC circuit analysis.
